title: EnFractal shared definitions
description: Shared building blocks for every EnFractal contract. Units are metres, kilograms, seconds and degrees. Coordinates follow Godot: +Y up, -Z forward, right-handed. The .invalid host is deliberate: these identifiers are never fetched.

token.description: Lowercase identifier for rooms, assets, presets, spawns, openings, jobs and parts.

action_id.description: Client-chosen idempotency key for one command. Same principal + same action_id + same content replays the original receipt; different content is refused.

entity_id.description: Namespaced entity identity. shell: room shell part; obj: captured or authored object instance; creation: compiled creation instance; avatar: player or companion body; effect: running effect; edit: legacy world_state entity.

principal_id.description: Who issued an action. Assigned by the trusted adapter, never accepted from a request body.

rel_path.description: Relative POSIX path inside the owning room or asset directory. No '.', '..' or empty segments, no trailing slash, backslashes, schemes or absolute paths, so one file has exactly one spelling.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative POSIX path, used only for documentation and reference-image pointers.

vec3.description: Three finite coordinates in metres, bounded to keep float32 runtimes and hashes stable.

quat_xyzw.description: Rotation quaternion in Godot order (x, y, z, w). Must be unit length; validators check this.

scale.description: Uniform scale. Captured assets are generated at true size, so this is 1 unless a player or magic resized the entity.

material_role.description: What a surface is made of. The style preset maps each role to a painterly treatment; physics may map it to friction and sound.

affordance.description: Semantic interaction hints. Whether a given body can carry or climb something is decided at runtime from size, mass and the actor's profile.

preset_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the preset file bytes (UTF-8, LF line endings).

extensions.description: Escape hatch for experiments. Keys must start with x_ and name the owning lane, for example x_look_rimlight. The integrator promotes a key into the schema or removes it; consumers must ignore keys they do not understand.

glb_path.description: A self-contained binary glTF: every buffer and image is embedded (no external or data URIs other than data:), so the file's hash pins all of its content.

display_text.description: Single-line text shown to people and models: names, categories, labels, notes. Treated as untrusted data wherever it comes from. Control, line-separator, zero-width, bidirectional-override and other invisible characters (the soft hyphen, the Arabic letter mark, Hangul fillers, variation selectors U+FE00-U+FE0D, interlinear annotation marks, the TAG block and the rest of plane 14) are forbidden so it cannot fake structure or hide text. The four emoji markers (VS15 U+FE0E, VS16 U+FE0F, the zero-width joiner U+200D and the keycap combiner U+20E3) pass the pattern but are allowed only where an emoji puts them: a selector directly after an Extended_Pictographic character or 0-9, # or *, one per base; the joiner between two emoji; the keycap after 0-9, # or *, optionally with VS16. A pattern cannot express that context, so readers check it in code (contracts/validate.py, RoomData.cs, the companion). The pattern is ECMA-262: '$' matches only at the very end. A UTF-16 reader refuses plane 14 through \uDB40-\uDB7F; a reader that matches code points refuses U+E0000-U+EFFFF in code (contracts/validate.py).

long_text.description: Multi-line untrusted text (descriptions, review notes, prompts). Newline and tab are the only control characters allowed; the invisible characters display_text forbids are forbidden here too, and the emoji markers are allowed only in place, as there.

request_id.description: Host-minted, unguessable identifier (at least 128 bits, lowercase hex).
